newsitem.title: GERMANY: Conti testing cost-cutting tyre machinery.
newsitem.headline: Conti testing cost-cutting tyre machinery.

text.p: German tyre-maker Continental AG, still glowing in the wake of a stellar earnings report, said on Monday it was installing new machinery that could sharply cut production costs.
Conti, which last week reported a 73 percent jump in first half pretax profit, said it would test 30 prototypes of machines developed with Krupp Elastomertechnik GmbH.

The machines automate several production steps and can be quickly reset to make different types of tyres, reducing costs and possibly jobs. They would be used at locations in the United States and Europe.
Earlier this year, Conti downplayed the impact of the machines, saying they would not have a major effect on the company or its workforce for several more years.

The company at that time also said the machinery could make tyre production in Germany and the U.S. competitive with production in low-wage countries such as India. Conti has recently cut costs by moving some production out of Germany to the Czech Republic and Ireland.
On August 11, Conti said improved efficiency helped spur pretax profit to soar to 208 million marks. Sales in the first six months of 1997 rose five percent to 5.35 billion marks.
